chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the honor of a man for his Muslim brother is that he accepts his gift and reciprocates with what he has, and he does not burden him with anything.'

key_terms.يُتْحِفُهُ: He gifts him / He reciprocates with a gift

ai.seo_question: What are the key etiquettes of gift-giving and receiving in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the social dimension of charity by framing gift exchange as a means of preserving dignity and fostering brotherhood. It instructs believers to accept gifts graciously to honor the giver, reciprocate appropriately without extravagance, and avoid creating financial or emotional burdens, thereby strengthening communal bonds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the honouring of the man to his Muslim brother is that he accepts his gifts and gifts him with what is with him, and he does not burden anything for him’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Isma’il ibn Mehran from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
would use gifts for food but not charity and he would say, “You must exchange gifts, it gently removes resentment and clears grudges due to animosity and malice.’””
